notes: Produced a controller with slightly narrower sensor spread ±0.035 m, increased integral gain ki to 1.2, and reduced base speed to 1.0 based on race data showing off-track failures and line loss. Expected to improve stability and completion rates.
rationale: The evidence from the last races shows that narrowing the sensor spread to ±0.04 m with sensor size 0.016 m improved control stability and reduced noise compared to wider spreads, but the robot still failed to complete the tracks, losing the line once per run and going off track before finishing. The integral gain ki at 1.0 helped reduce steady-state error, but the base speed of 1.05 was still somewhat aggressive, leading to off-track failures. To further improve stability and line detection consistency, I narrowed the sensor spread slightly to ±0.035 m, keeping the sensor size at 0.016 m to maintain robust detection. I increased ki to 1.2 to enhance integral correction and reduce steady-state error, and lowered base_speed to 1.0 to balance control and progress, reducing the risk of overshoot and off-track events. The controller gains kp and kd remain at 9.0 and 1.2 respectively, with sensor weights scaled to the sensor positions. The line loss strategy remains 'search_left' to steer right on line loss. I request observations of completion, progress, line_loss_events, rms_error, and completion_time to monitor improvements. I expect these changes to reduce line loss events, improve completion rates, and enhance accuracy on complex tracks, especially the s-bend.
